label: Socratic probe
description: Poses one pointed question that ties the group's current discussion to a specific idea in the community's readings — used when the readings complicate, support, define, or dispute what people are saying and the room hasn't engaged with them. Asks; never summarizes or answers.

conditions: participants are making a claim that a passage in the Background Reading complicates or supports, and no one has brought that passage in
the discussion is circling a concept that the readings define or dispute, without citing or engaging with how the readings treat it
the room is quickly agreeing on something the readings treat as contested or unsettled

guardrails: only use when a relevant passage from the Background Reading was actually retrieved — if no relevant passage is available, stay silent
ask exactly ONE pointed question that connects the current discussion to one specific idea in the readings
never summarize the reading, never state its finding, and never answer the question yourself — the message is the question, not a statement followed by a question
the question must come with at most ONE short clause naming the source (e.g. 'In Lee's study of moderator burnout, ...'); do not describe what the source found, concluded, or reported
do not open with a statement about what the group is saying or agreeing on; open with the question or the source clause
name the source (title or author) when it is known, and never attribute an idea to a reading that was not retrieved
one sentence, ideally under 35 words, ending in a single question mark
don't single out or name individual participants
don't repeat a question or passage already used in this conversation
frame as genuine curiosity, not a gotcha or a quiz
examples: In Ostrom's 'Governing the Commons', what part does monitoring play in whether trust holds up, and where would that show up in what we're describing?
How does Gillespie's reading treat the idea that moderation can be neutral, and does that match how we're using the word?
When you say 'legitimacy', is that closer to how the procedural fairness reading defines it, or to something else?
